claim: `syntax:` / `contexts:` give the VAR declaration as `Name BYTE [Count]` (and `Declaration: BYTE [Count]`). Spin2 VAR is `BYTE Name[Count]`; this is the root of defect class var-declaration-name-before-type (the three example blocks).

CALL and REGEXEC are documented as returning a long ('result := CALL(PASMAddress)', 'Value returned in result1 register', 'Result in result1 register'); the source lists neither with a result and the compiler rejects them as expression terms ('Expression terms must return a single result'). `result1` is not a defined symbol. regexec.yaml:36-37,41 also claims the routine 'Can be > 512 longs / loaded and executed in chunks / can execute code larger than cog RAM'; the source describes REGEXEC as loading ONE self-defined chunk (header `WORD start, finish-start-1`, then `ORG`) into cog registers, and none of the three examples shows that header. Related notes (call.yaml:44-47 'Parameters passed via PTRA/PTRB', 'Preserves Spin2 interpreter state') are not in the source.

GETRND is described as a 'hardware random number generator' with 'true entropy ... true random based on thermal noise ... suitable for cryptographic use'. The source says GETRND returns from the xoroshiro128** PRNG, seeded at boot with thermal noise. (Also getrnd.yaml:104,129 give '2-9 cycles' for the method call; no source states it.)

'Calculate CRC using hardware CRC engine', 'Uses P2's hardware CRC engine', 'Fast hardware implementation', 'Initial CRC value is 0'. The source says only: 'Compute a CRC of Count bytes starting at BytePtr using a custom polynomial of up to 32 bits.'

`value := sqrt(-1.0)  ' Creates NaN` and note 'Examples: 0.0/0.0, sqrt(-1), inf-inf'. SQRT is the UNSIGNED INTEGER square-root operator (the -1.0 float bit pattern is just a large unsigned number; the result is an integer, not NaN). The float square root is FSQRT.

QLOG/QEXP are described as natural log / e^x (examples 'ln(0.0625)', 'e^1 in 5.27 format', 'Convert ln to log10', `QEXP(x * 22713 >> 13)  ' 10^x using e^(x*ln(10))`). The silicon instructions are log base 2 and 2^x; exp2.yaml:60 and log2.yaml:11,63 already say EXP2/LOG2 use QEXP/QLOG, so the KB contradicts itself. The 39457>>17 factor in qlog.yaml:22 (= log10(2)) only works for a base-2 log; the 22713 constant in qexp.yaml:22 equals neither ln(10)*8192 (18864) nor log2(10)*8192 (27213). The 'Input range 0.0625 to 2.0 / Output range' notes (qlog.yaml:30, qexp.yaml:31,33) are unsourced.

`%%1032` is documented as 'Swap adjacent pairs: $12_34_56_78 -> $34_12_78_56' (pattern table and the swap_pairs example). MOVBYTS D = {D.BYTE[S[7:6]], D.BYTE[S[5:4]], D.BYTE[S[3:2]], D.BYTE[S[1:0]]}, so %%1032 gives $56_78_12_34 (a WORD swap). The pairs-of-bytes swap $34_12_78_56 is %%2301. The other table rows (%%0123, %%3210, %%0000, %%3333, %%0321, %%2103) check out.
`HUBSET($8000_0000)  ' Bit 31 = reset chip` -- a HUBSET operand with the MSB set seeds 32 bits of the PRNG; the chip reset is `HUBSET ##$1000_0000`.

The five WRPIN mode literals have 31 digits (4+4+3+13+2+5); the documented mode word is `%AAAA_BBBB_FFF_MMMMMMMMMMMMM_TT_SSSSS_0` (32 bits, SSSSS at bits 5:1, wrpin.yaml:28 itself says 'Bit 0: Always 0'), so each SSSSS lands one bit low. The mode selectors are also wrong: UART TX uses SSSSS=00111 (async serial transmit is %11110), ADC uses 10011 (ADC is %11000).

wxpin.yaml:46 gives the sync-serial word size as X[5:0]; the source field is X.[4..0] (bits minus 1). Example `WXPIN(spi_pin, %1_00111)  ' 16 bits, MSB first`: X.[4..0]=7 means 8 bits (pinstart.yaml:90 correctly calls the same value '8 bits'); 16 bits is 15. (wxpin.yaml:77 NCO example `freq * ($8000_0000 / (CLKFREQ / 2))` also truncates the 2^32/CLKFREQ factor -- at 200 MHz 21 instead of 21.47, a 2% error; low severity.)
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/silicon-doc/silicon-doc-text.txt:4654, :4675 (X.[4..0] sets the number of bits, minus 1; 7 = 8 bits)

claim: MaxCount is documented as including the terminator ('Max 79 chars + null' for 80; 'Stops at source null or MaxCount-1 characters'; 'Destination buffer must be at least MaxCount bytes'). The source: Max is the maximum number of CHARACTERS copied, and the copied string occupies up to Max+1 bytes including the zero. As written, a buffer sized per the page overflows by one byte.
'Escape sequences supported (\n, \t, etc.)' for STRING(). The source gives backslash escapes only for the `@\"text\n\"` form; STRING("Text",13) takes quoted characters plus numeric values.

RECV and SEND are special method pointers that are ASSIGNED (`SEND := @OutMethod`, `RECV := @InMethod`) and inherited by called methods; the pages instead document copying them OUT into a LONG (`outputMethod := SEND`, `inputMethod := RECV`) and calling that, which is not how the source describes them. (The example's call `inputMethod()` also lacks the `:1` result count -- defect class method-pointer-call-without-result-count.) The restriction lists ('Cannot use abort syntax with RECV/SEND') have no source.

COGINIT is called with NEWCOG. NEWCOG is the COGSPIN symbol; COGINIT's symbols are COGEXEC_NEW / HUBEXEC_NEW / ..._PAIR (coginit.yaml:20-26 itself lists them). Both are %01_0000 so the code compiles and runs, but it is the wrong symbol for the method.

'Use predefined clkmode_ constants'. The only predefined names are `clkmode_` (the compiled clock mode) and `clkmode`; the examples' clkmode_pll / clkmode_rcfast do not exist (defect class undefined-clkmode-constants).
`underlying_pasm.description: "Direct access to CNT register"` -- CNT is the Propeller 1 counter register; the P2 has no CNT (the counter is read with GETCT).
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/spin2-v55/spin2-v55-text.txt:547 (GETCT); same page lines 9-20 state the P2 64-bit CT

claim: 'Blocks execution until system counter matches Tick value' and timing 'Waits until exact counter match' contradict the page's own description (lines 4-8): the wait ends when the MSB of (CT - Tick) is 0, i.e. once CT has PASSED Tick, not on an exact match.
source: engineering/ingestion/sources/spin2-v55/spin2-v55-text.txt:549 ('Wait for system counter to get past Tick')

claim: 'Cannot signal yourself (no effect)'. The silicon description ORs every cog's strobe outputs and delivers the composite to each cog by bit; it does not exclude the signalling cog, and the same page's example `COGATN($FF ^ (1 << COGID()))` implies self is otherwise included.

BYTEMOVE/WORDMOVE/LONGMOVE are documented as overlap-safe with automatic direction choice (and examples such as `BYTEMOVE(@array[1], @array[0], 49)` depend on it). The source says only 'Move Count bytes/words/longs from Source to Destination'. Needs an empirical run (EF ledger) before the claim stands; until then it is unsourced.

Beyond the registered S-006 (syntax lacks Count), the descriptions/parameters describe a swap of two single values ('Swap byte values between two memory locations'; parameters Address1/Address2 only) and the notes claim 'Atomically exchanges the values', 'Efficient single-operation exchange'. The source swaps COUNT elements of two ranges; nothing says atomic.

`send(BYTE($48, $65, $6C, $6C, $6F))  ' "Hello"` is presented as passing a byte string to a user method, but Spin2 names are case-insensitive: `send` is the built-in SEND method pointer, so the example compiles by calling it. The comparable long.yaml:41 `calculate(...)` and word.yaml:41 `process(...)` do not collide.

Specific behavioural claims with no source in v55 (low confidence, listed for the register only): 'Cog 0 always starts first at boot'; 'Cannot stop cog -1 (no effect)'; 'Values outside 0-7 return 0'; 'Maximum 496 longs can be loaded'.
